content.thinking:
I'm laying out the design decisions in execution order, each tied to its ticket: starting with the foundational model choice to use anchors instead of branches (COR-2110), then keeping distill as a feeder that funnels into the fact store.

From there I'm sequencing through checkpoint events replacing session-end triggers (COR-2127), commit stamping from a fact's own checkpoint via trailer rather than HEAD (COR-2126), sessionID stamping, per-fact storage with anchors replacing branch heads, trail_id stamping at merge, and a per-fact client with reachability-filtered pull replacing lineage.json.

I'm finishing with the read-time join logic for the repo page (COR-2124), the repo pool with no special UX, UI placement decisions (COR-2125), dropping local transcript caching in favor of reading from git (COR-2128), and finally the derived rules around closed-unmerged trails and auto repo-visibility on merge, keeping each decision to one sentence with its Linear ticket link.

content.text:
1. **A memory is keyed by its provenance anchors (session + checkpoint + commit), never by branch name; every surface is a query over anchors** — [COR-2110](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110/design-how-memories-attach-to-trails-upload-scope-triggers-edge-cases)
2. **Distill stays as-is and, with `remember`, funnels into one local fact store that pushes to brainstore on post-commit** — [COR-2110](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110/design-how-memories-attach-to-trails-upload-scope-triggers-edge-cases)
3. **The checkpoint event (post-commit hook → host `brainnotify` → plugin notify) is the primary trigger for both distill and sync; session-end is deprecated and nothing new depends on it** — [COR-2127](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2127/checkpoint-event-host-brainnotify-plugin-primary-trigger-for-distill)
4. **Distill stamps `Anchor.Commit` resolved from the fact's own checkpoint via the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, never from HEAD, and leaves it blank when unresolvable** — [COR-2126](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces)
5. **`remember` gains a `--session` flag (plus env fallback) so agent-authored facts carry a SessionID; a human in a terminal legitimately has none** — [COR-2126](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces)
6. **Brainstore stores per-fact rows keyed `(repo_id, fact_id)` with anchor rows, dropping branch-keyed set heads and CAS entirely** — [COR-2123](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123/brainstore-per-fact-storage-with-anchors-upsert-delta-feed-endpoints)
7. **The delta feed uses the platform-standard opaque cursor / `next_cursor` pagination (the existing `/memories` keyset shape), with cursor-less replay as the resync path** — [COR-2123](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123/brainstore-per-fact-storage-with-anchors-upsert-delta-feed-endpoints)
8. **`trail_id` is stamped on facts at trail merge and on late upserts whose anchors belong to an already-merged trail, as a materialized cache of the anchor join** — [COR-2123](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123/brainstore-per-fact-storage-with-anchors-upsert-delta-feed-endpoints)
9. **The plugin replaces branch-head sync with idempotent per-fact push and a pull filtered locally by HEAD reachability / own session / merged `trail_id` / pool, which also fixes teammate distribution with no promote step; `lineage.json` is cancelled** — [COR-2126](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces)
10. **The attachment join runs in the BFF at read time: trail page = anchors ∩ trail membership, repo page = commits core marks on-default + merged `trail_id` + pool** — [COR-2124](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2124/memorytrail-attachment-join-resolve-facts-to-trailsrepo-page-via)
11. **Pool facts get no special UX — ordinary rows with null session/checkpoint/commit columns** — [COR-2124](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2124/memorytrail-attachment-join-resolve-facts-to-trailsrepo-page-via)
12. **Anchor precision is measured on existing facts before per-commit rendering is built, with trail-level rendering as the fallback for historical facts** — [COR-2124](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2124/memorytrail-attachment-join-resolve-facts-to-trailsrepo-page-via)
13. **Trail UI renders memories beside their anchoring commits and the repo Memories page shows only main-visible facts, all behind the `trail-memories` flag; merged trails keep their memories forever, closed-unmerged trails' facts never reach the repo page** — [COR-2125](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2125/trail-ui-memories-beside-commits-repo-memories-page-anchor-joins)
14. **The local transcript cache is removed — transcripts are read from the git checkpoint refs on demand, with transient materialization only for backfill** — [COR-2128](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2128/entire-brain-remove-the-local-transcript-cache-read-transcripts-from)

content.thinking:
Starting on COR-2127, the checkpoint event ticket for the brainnotify-to-plugin trigger. I'm moving it to In Progress in Linear, and noting that I should track this workflow rule—moving each ticket through its stages—in the tracker file header for future reference.

Looking at the scope, this spans two repos: the host side in entireio/cli needs brainnotify re-cut from an unmerged branch, while the plugin side in this workspace needs the checkpoint hint wired in. I'm weighing whether to work directly in the ~/code/entire/cli checkout versus staying confined to my designated workspace, since touching another repo's state could conflict with the user's own checkout.

Given this is now implementation work across two repos, I should check the branch's staleness against main first, start with the safer plugin-side change here, and follow test-driven-development practices per the superpowers guidance.

The repo guide requires a brain brief for this task, a graph preflight check, and focused source reading before touching exported symbols. I'll move the ticket to In Progress, update the tracker, do the brain brief, then investigate both the stale branch's diff on the cli side and the memory notify handler on the plugin side before presenting a short implementation plan.

Since the user already gave explicit go-ahead, I can proceed into investigation and implementation directly rather than pausing for more confirmation. The cli branch is two months stale, but the notify package is small, so re-cutting it against current main should be manageable — I need to trace where the original branch called Notify from and check throttling behavior on the plugin side.

For throttling, the worker already has a 15-minute throttle for hostedFactsSync on watch ticks, so for checkpoint-triggered syncs I should probably use a shorter throttle (maybe 60s) via a timestamp file, similar pattern but tighter. I'm also considering whether distill can meaningfully run on an in-progress session given the notify payload carries a session id — distill caches by transcript fingerprint, so a changed transcript would trigger re-distillation, but I'm unsure if distill actually supports mid-session distillation yet.

Running full re-distillation on every checkpoint commit is a real concern since the cache is keyed on whole-session fingerprints, meaning each commit could reprocess the entire growing transcript and burn tokens unnecessarily unless there's chunk-level caching I'm missing — I need to check how the session cache is actually structured before deciding.

So for COR-2127, the plugin-side scope splits into wiring notify to a throttled sync, which is straightforward, versus making checkpoint-triggered distill avoid quadratic token cost, which isn't solved yet without a delta mechanism. The decision that checkpoints drive both distill and sync means this delta requirement can't be deferred.

Given the size of this, my plan is to investigate thoroughly first—the CLI branch, the plugin's notify path, and whether distill can be incremental—then report back a concrete plan, likely split into sub-parts, before implementing. Since the user said to start, doing the investigation and presenting a plan counts as real progress, and I can move into implementation once the plugin wiring looks clean.

Concretely I'll mark COR-2127 as In Progress and update the tracker header, pull the required brain brief for this ticket work, diff the feat/brain-lifecycle-hints branch against its merge-base to see what changed and where it's called, then dig into the plugin's memory notify handler and worker to find the right wiring point and check whether distill's incremental state supports delta updates.

The checkpoint event becomes the **primary** trigger for both distill and fact sync. Session-end is being deprecated (developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never); nothing new may depend on it.

**Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

1. `entire enable` installs a post-commit git hook that runs `entire hooks git post-commit` — this is the existing checkpoint-capture path in the host CLI.
2. Inside that flow the host calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. Detached and never-fails by design: a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. This host half exists on the **unmerged** entireio/cli branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` (commit 73a92e8da) — land or re-cut it.
3. The plugin endpoint (`entire brain memory notify`, on main in `internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`) records a content-free hint and nudges the plugin's worker.
4. The worker runs, throttled: distill the transcript delta since the previous checkpoint (anchoring facts to the checkpoint window they came from — better precision than session-end distill, which lumps the whole session onto its last checkpoint), then push the fact store.

This ticket can land first.

I've confirmed distill caching works on a whole-session fingerprint, so a growing transcript means every chunk gets re-run, making naive checkpoint-triggered distill quadratic in tokens over long sessions. That splits the ticket's plugin work into two tiers: syncing on checkpoint is cheap and safe to do now, but distilling on checkpoint needs chunk-level or line-watermark incrementality to avoid that quadratic blowup.

Since chunks are content-split by byte limits, earlier chunk boundaries stay stable as a transcript appends, only the final partial chunk changes, so a per-chunk cache keyed by chunk content hash would give natural incrementality: reuse unchanged chunks and only call the agent for new or changed ones. The complication is that fact retirement, force/rebuild paths, and cache purges all assume session-level granularity, so this would be a moderate but contained change localized to the distill command pipeline and its cache layer.

For COR-2127, I'm thinking of splitting the work into three parts: recutting the brainnotify/checkpoint call site on the host CLI side, making the plugin's checkpoint notify trigger a throttled hosted facts sync (possibly gated by affordability), and building chunk-level incremental distill in the plugin so checkpoint-triggered distill stays linear rather than reprocessing the whole session each time. The third part is the real prerequisite — without it, even throttled per-checkpoint distill would be wastefully quadratic, whereas with a chunk cache each commit only costs the price of processing the new tail chunk, and it also has the side benefit of anchoring facts to whichever checkpoint the new chunk actually belongs to.

Given how much scope and token-spend this implies, I don't want to plow ahead silently — I should surface the plan to the user and get a quick ack first, since there are real decisions to make: what throttle value to use for the checkpoint sync (I'd propose 60s), whether to build the chunk-level cache now or defer the distill trigger until after that's done, and how the CLI-side work should be sequenced relative to the rest.

content.text:
Investigation done — the plan for COR-2127 has one real scope decision in it, so here it is before I write code:

**What I found:**

1. **Host side (entireio/cli):** the stale branch splits cleanly. Only `brainnotify/` (60 lines + tests) and the call sites matter; the rest of `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` is unrelated checkpoint-discovery work. The checkpoint call site is `ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit` — it fires the hint only for sessions that actually condensed into the new checkpoint, which is exactly right. I'd re-cut just that onto current main and wire **only the checkpoint event** (dropping the session-start/end call sites — session-end is deprecated).
2. **Plugin sync on checkpoint:** cheap and safe. `memory notify --event checkpoint` already records a hint and launches the worker; adding a throttled `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` there (propose: 60s min interval via timestamp file, same pattern as the watch throttle) is a small contained change.
3. **Plugin distill on checkpoint — the catch:** distill's cache is a **whole-session fingerprint** (`distill_cmd.go:1961`). A growing session re-runs *every* chunk on each distill, so naively distilling per commit is quadratic in tokens over a long session. The fix is natural though: chunks are split from the start of the transcript, so an appending transcript keeps earlier chunk boundaries stable — a **per-chunk cache** (keyed by chunk content hash) makes per-commit distill re-process only the new tail chunk. Bonus: tail chunks distilled at checkpoint time anchor to the *current* checkpoint, which is precisely the anchor-precision improvement the design promised.

**Proposed split:**
- **A** — cli: new branch, re-cut `brainnotify` + checkpoint call site + tests, PR to entireio/cli.
- **B** — plugin: checkpoint hint → throttled facts sync (60s), PR to entire-brain.
- **C** — plugin: per-chunk distill cache, then enable distill-on-checkpoint. Without C, I'd wire the trigger but leave distill on tick/session-end to avoid the quadratic spend.

The scope question: **do C inside COR-2127** (complete the ticket as designed, ~the largest of the three parts), or ship A+B now and split C into its own ticket? I'd do A+B+C under this ticket since "distill is checkpoint-triggered" is the decision we recorded, but C touches distill's cache model, which you may want as a separately reviewable change.

One logistics note: part A means working in `~/code/entire/cli` directly (new branch off main) — your checkout is clean; say if you'd rather I not touch it.

I need to answer three clarifying questions precisely based on the actual code before implementing, including the detail that each PR/trail gets attached to COR-2127 via Linear links. Looking at the brainnotify mechanism, I'm checking the notify function's signature and its guard clause that skips execution when the ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER environment variable is set to 1.

The notification works by re-invoking the entire CLI as a detached subprocess that calls itself through the brain plugin dispatcher, spawning fire-and-forget with no wait or result reading — so failures are invisible by design, relying on canonical reconciliation to catch missed hints. This fires from ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit once a session's checkpoint condense succeeds, tied to the worktree path and branch. Now I need to verify whether this notification mechanism actually launches the worker process itself, or just signals it.

So tracing through: `memory notify` writes a content-free hint record under the brain dir, then launches the detached memory worker if not already running, guarded by a coordinator lease. But crucially, that worker today only does conversation-indexing for retrieval — it doesn't distill and doesn't touch brainstore at all. The plan's hosted facts sync step just pushes whatever facts are already sitting in the local store from prior distills; it won't surface new facts from the just-committed work until a distill actually runs.

I'm thinking the sync should probably live in the notify handler itself right after recording the hint, throttled, with a never-fails discipline — since notify is already detached from the host hook, a few extra seconds there is fine.

For the per-chunk distill end-to-end plan, I'm sketching out extending the distillCache entry to also store chunk content hashes alongside the session fingerprint, so when a session's transcript grows, I can diff chunk hashes against the previous entry and skip agent calls for chunks already distilled — content-ID dedupe makes this safe even on re-run, only truly new or changed chunks need processing.

I also need to verify chunking is deterministic and prefix-stable: since chunking splits by max bytes from the start, appending turns should leave earlier chunks byte-identical except the last partial one, which grows until it hits the boundary — though I need to watch for the case where preprocessing rewrites earlier content, since each checkpoint re-exports the full transcript.

If condensation does rewrite history, those chunks' hashes change and they'll correctly re-distill, just at some token cost. For anchor stamping, since new chunks get the current checkpoint while already-distilled chunks keep their original facts, anchors should converge to per-window precision over time. For trigger wiring, I'm thinking the checkpoint handler needs to run a throttled incremental export of the session transcript, then kick off a per-session distill pass.

I'm also budgeting guards by reusing distill's abort/threshold logic, throttling, and skipping when a distill lock is held, while reconciliation only touches new facts and retirement is governed by force-rebuild and salt-based chunk cache invalidation. The overall flow runs: commit triggers a post-commit hook that captures a checkpoint, writes the transcript into git, and spawns a detached memory-notify process scoped to that session and branch.

The plugin then nudges the worker to export the transcript delta, distill only the new tail chunks anchored to the latest checkpoint, and sync/publish facts so the trail page reflects new commits within seconds — and each PR/trail should get linked back to COR-2127. Given the user's three questions are really confirmations of mechanism, I should answer them directly and then propose starting implementation with part A in a new CLI branch.

Doing A properly—porting the package, adapting drifted call sites, running tests, and formatting—is a meaty but worthwhile task for this turn. content.text:
The cli full-suite build/test run is chugging in the background (big repo — I'll pick up the result when it lands). Meanwhile, your three questions:

**A — the brainnotify mechanism.** It's a detached, content-free re-invocation of the CLI itself. Inside `PostCommit`, after a session actually condenses into the new checkpoint, the host calls `brainnotify.Notify(repoRoot, EventCheckpoint, sessionID, branch)`, which builds the argv `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id> --branch <b>` and runs it via `execx.SpawnDetached` — fire-and-forget, no wait, no output read. So: no socket, no queue, no file protocol — the "event bus" is literally spawning the plugin through the host's own plugin dispatcher, carrying only routing metadata (event, session id, branch). Three guards make it safe: it skips when invoked *from* the worker (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER=1`, loop prevention), it never affects the hook's result (a missing/broken plugin can't touch the commit), and a lost hint costs only freshness because the plugin's reconciliation pass remains authoritative.

**B — "launches the worker" clarified: no, it is not the distill worker.** Today `memory notify` does exactly two things: records the hint in a durable work record, and launches (if not already running, via a coordinator lease) the detached **memory worker** — which only does conversation indexing (transcript → retrieval exchanges). It never distills and never talks to brainstore. Part B adds the missing piece: in the checkpoint-event path, also run a throttled `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` — which pushes whatever facts are *already in the local store* (from earlier distills and `remember`s) to brainstore and pulls the head back. So after B alone: commit → facts already distilled reach brainstore within seconds; facts from the *just-committed* work still wait for the next distill. Part C closes that last gap.

**C — end to end.** Commit → checkpoint cp_n captured → detached notify → plugin (throttled, under the existing distill pass lock): (1) refresh this session's exported transcript, (2) distill it — the new part: the cache entry stores **per-chunk content hashes** alongside the session fingerprint, and since chunks split from the transcript's start, an appended transcript keeps earlier chunks byte-identical — only the new tail chunk(s) miss the cache and hit the model. Facts from those tail chunks anchor to **cp_n** and its commit (the window they actually came from — the precision win). (3) `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` publishes the store. Net cost per commit: roughly one agent call on the new transcript tail instead of re-processing the whole session; a rewritten history (condense/compaction) changes earlier chunk hashes and honestly re-distills them. Edge cases: salt (prompt/model/taxonomy) is part of the chunk hash so config changes invalidate everything, force-rebuild stays session-level, and content-ID dedupe means even a redundant re-distill can't duplicate facts.

Status: **part A is code-complete on `evis/cor-2127-brain-checkpoint-hint` in entireio/cli** — `brainnotify` package ported (its tests pass), one call site in `PostCommit` gated on the `condensed` result (main's existing signal), both call-site tests pass (hint per condensed session; no hint when condensation is skipped). I dropped the third old test (failure injection) — its helper no longer exists and the no-hint path it guarded is the same `condensed=false` branch test 2 covers. Once the full build/tests finish I'll push, open the PR, and attach the trail to COR-2127, then move to part B.

The entire-brain plugin currently learns about new work only at session end or on a daemon tick. Developers leave sessions running for days, so facts distilled from a commit's work can reach the trail long after review. This PR gives the plugin a per-commit signal: the moment a session condenses into a checkpoint, the host tells Brain, and Brain can distill + sync on that beat. Part of COR-2127 (hosted memory: checkpoint-event trigger); design on COR-2110.

## What changed

- New \`brainnotify\` package: \`Notify(repoRoot, event, sessionID, branch)\` spawns a detached \`entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id> --branch <b>\`. Content-free routing metadata only. Skips when invoked from the Brain worker itself (loop prevention), on empty repo/session, or on an unknown event.
- One call site: \`ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit\` fires the hint per session whose condensation actually produced the checkpoint, keyed on the existing \`condensed\` result.

Never-fails by construction: the spawn is detached, its result is never read, and a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. A lost hint costs freshness only — Brain's reconciliation pass stays authoritative.

Re-cut from \`feat/brain-lifecycle-hints\` (73a92e8da), taking only the brainnotify package and the checkpoint call site. The session-start/end call sites are deliberately not wired: session-end is being deprecated as a Brain trigger.

## Validation

- \`go test ./cmd/entire/cli/brainnotify ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy\` — pass (full strategy suite).
- \`go build ./...\` — pass.
- The old branch's third test (hint suppressed when condensation *fails*) depended on a removed helper (\`writeUnsupportedCheckpointPolicy\`); the path it guarded is the same \`condensed=false\` branch the skipped-condensation test covers, so it was dropped rather than re-inventing failure injection.

The checkpoint event becomes the **primary** trigger for both distill and fact sync. Session-end is being deprecated (developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never); nothing new may depend on it.

**Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

1. `entire enable` installs a post-commit git hook that runs `entire hooks git post-commit` — this is the existing checkpoint-capture path in the host CLI.
2. Inside that flow the host calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. 3. The plugin endpoint (`entire brain memory notify`, on main in `internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`) records a content-free hint and nudges the plugin's worker.
4. The worker runs, throttled: distill the transcript delta since the previous checkpoint (anchoring facts to the checkpoint window they came from — better precision than session-end distill, which lumps the whole session onto its last checkpoint), then push the fact store.

31	// seam over the same short-term delta the session-end hook runs.
32	var notifyCheckpointExport = func(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, opts Options, repoDir string) error {
33		sub := &cobra.Command{}
34		sub.SetContext(ctx)
35		sub.SetOut(errW)
36		sub.SetErr(errW)
37		_, err := watchShortTermDelta(ctx, sub, opts, repoDir)
38		return err
39	}
40	
41	// notifyCheckpointDistill distills the hinted session. The chunk cache makes
42	// this cheap per commit: chunking is prefix-stable, so only the transcript
43	// tail added since the previous checkpoint dispatches an agent call, and its
44	// facts anchor to the checkpoint that raised the hint. Test seam.
45	var notifyCheckpointDistill = func(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, opts Options, repoDir, sessionID string) error {
46		sub := &cobra.Command{}
47		sub.SetContext(ctx)
48		sub.SetOut(errW)
49		sub.SetErr(errW)
50		distillOpts := distillCommandOptions{
51			session:             sessionID,
52			agent:               "auto",
53			timeout:             defaultDistillTimeout,
54			maxChunkBytes:       defaultDistillChunkSize,
55			confidenceThreshold: defaultFactConfidenceThreshold,
56			concurrency:         defaultDistillConcurrency,
57		}
58		return runDistill(ctx, sub, opts, distillOpts, repoDir)
59	}
60	
61	type memoryNotifySyncMarker struct {
62		LastSyncAt time.Time `json:"last_sync_at"`
63	}
64	
65	// hostedSyncOnCheckpointHint runs the checkpoint-hint work: export the changed
66	// transcripts, distill the hinted session (tail chunks only, via the chunk
67	// cache), then sync the hinted branch and the default branch — throttled by a
68	// shared marker. The marker is claimed BEFORE the work so concurrent notify
69	// processes skip instead of stampeding; a failed run after the claim simply
70	// waits out the interval, which the never-fails contract already tolerates.
71	//
72	// Same contract as hostedFactsSyncAndPull: this runs behind a host lifecycle
73	// hint, so nothing here may fail the caller — every outcome is reported on
74	// errW and swallowed. The return value says whether the work ran, for tests
75	// and for the caller's log line only.
76	func hostedSyncOnCheckpointHint(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, opts Options, repoDir string, storage repoStorage, sessionID, branch string) bool {
77		claimed := false
78		if err := withBrainWriteLock(storage.BrainDir, func() error {
79			now := opts.Now().UTC()
80			marker := readMemoryNotifySyncMarker(storage.BrainDir)
81			if now.Sub(marker.LastSyncAt) < memoryNotifyHostedSyncMinInterval {
82				return nil
83			}
84			if err := writeMemoryNotifySyncMarker(storage.BrainDir, memoryNotifySyncMarker{LastSyncAt: now}); err != nil {
85				return err
86			}
87			claimed = true
88			return nil
89		}); err != nil {
90			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "memory notify: hosted sync throttle: %v\n", err)
91			return false
92		}
93		if !claimed {
94			return false
95		}
96	
97		// Export before distill: distill reads the exported transcript, and the
98		// checkpoint that raised this hint is exactly what the delta brings in.
99		// Both steps are best-effort; the sync still runs so facts already in the
100		// store reach the trail even when the agent is unavailable.
101		if err := notifyCheckpointExport(ctx, errW, opts, repoDir); err != nil {
102			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "memory notify: incremental export failed: %v\n", err)
103		}
104		if sessionID != "" {
105			if err := notifyCheckpointDistill(ctx, errW, opts, repoDir, sessionID); err != nil {
106				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "memory notify: distill skipped: %v\n", err)
107			}
108		}
109	
110		if branch == "" {
111			branch = hostedSyncBranch(ctx, opts.Runner, repoDir)
112		}
113		syncBranches := []string{branch}
114		if branch != distillDefaultBranch {
115			syncBranches = append(syncBranches, distillDefaultBranch)
116		}
117		for _, syncBranch := range syncBranches {
118			if err := notifyHostedFactsSync(ctx, errW, opts, repoDir, storage, syncBranch); err != nil {
119				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "memory notify: hosted fact sync failed (local brain unaffected): %v\n", err)
120			}
121		}
122		return true
123	}
124	
125	func memoryNotifySyncMarkerPath(brainDir string) string {
126		return filepath.Join(brainDir, memoryNotifySyncMarkerName)
127	}
128	
129	// readMemoryNotifySyncMarker treats a missing or unreadable marker as "never
130	// synced": the worst outcome of a corrupt marker is one extra sync.
131	func readMemoryNotifySyncMarker(brainDir string) memoryNotifySyncMarker {
132		var marker memoryNotifySyncMarker
133		data, err := os.ReadFile(memoryNotifySyncMarkerPath(brainDir))
134		if err != nil {
135			return memoryNotifySyncMarker{}
136		}
137		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &marker); err != nil {
138			return memoryNotifySyncMarker{}
139		}
140		return marker
141	}
142	
143	func writeMemoryNotifySyncMarker(brainDir string, marker memoryNotifySyncMarker) error {
144		data, err := json.Marshal(marker)
145		if err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		return os.WriteFile(memoryNotifySyncMarkerPath(brainDir), data, 0o600)
149	}

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --title "Checkpoint hint triggers throttled distill + hosted fact sync (COR-2127)" --body "## Why

Facts currently reach brainstore only at session end or on a daemon tick, and developers leave sessions running for days — so a trail under review shows no memories from the work being reviewed. The host CLI now sends a detached checkpoint hint per commit (entireio/cli#2784); this PR makes the plugin act on it, so facts appear on the trail during review. Part of COR-2127; design on COR-2110 (v3). Session-end is being deprecated as a trigger and nothing here depends on it.

## What changed

- **\`hostedSyncOnCheckpointHint\`** (\`internal/cli/memory_notify_sync.go\`): on a \`checkpoint\` hint — claim a shared 60s throttle marker under the brain write lock (claim-first, so concurrent detached notifies skip instead of stampeding), then export changed transcripts, distill the hinted session, and run the existing \`hostedFactsSyncAndPull\` for the hinted branch + default branch. Never-fails: every outcome prints to stderr and returns nil; a missing agent still syncs whatever is already in the store.
- **Per-chunk distill cache** (\`distill_cmd.go\`): the cache gains a \`chunks\` map recording each session's salted chunk content hashes. Chunking is prefix-stable, so a transcript grown by one commit re-dispatches only the new tail chunk — per-commit distill is linear in new content, not quadratic in session length — and the tail's facts anchor to the checkpoint that raised the hint. \`--force\` bypasses reuse (it drops the facts it is about to regenerate). Privacy purge clears chunk records alongside session entries. Old cache files load unchanged; reuse starts after their next distill.

- \`gofmt -s\`, \`go vet\` clean.

## Risk

Distill now runs per commit (throttled to once/60s) instead of per session end. Token spend is bounded by the chunk cache: each chunk of a session is distilled once in total, same as before — the spend moves earlier, it does not grow. A rewritten transcript history (condense/compaction) changes chunk hashes and honestly re-distills those chunks.

# COR-2110 table of truth

Tracks the approved decisions and their tickets. Cross a row off (strikethrough + ✅) when its ticket ships, and move the ticket through the Linear stages as work progresses (In Progress when started, In Review at PR, Done when shipped). Work order: COR-2127 → COR-2126 → COR-2123 → COR-2124 → COR-2125, with COR-2128 independent.

Current: COR-2127 — In Progress (started 2026-10-15).

| # | Decision | Ticket | Status |
|---|----------|--------|--------|
| 1 | A memory is keyed by its provenance anchors (session + checkpoint + commit), never by branch name; every surface is a query over anchors | [COR-2110](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110) | ☐ design (done when all below ship) |
| 2 | Distill stays as-is and, with `remember`, funnels into one local fact store that pushes to brainstore on post-commit | [COR-2110](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110) | ☐ |
| 3 | Checkpoint event (post-commit hook → host `brainnotify` → plugin notify) is the primary trigger for distill and sync; session-end deprecated | [COR-2127](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2127) | ☐ |
| 4 | Distill stamps `Anchor.Commit` from the fact's own checkpoint via the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, never HEAD; blank when unresolvable | [COR-2126](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126) | ☐ |
| 5 | `remember` gains `--session` (+ env fallback) so agent-authored facts carry a SessionID; absent stays valid for humans | [COR-2126](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126) | ☐ |
| 6 | Brainstore stores per-fact rows `(repo_id, fact_id)` with anchor rows; branch-keyed set heads and CAS dropped | [COR-2123](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123) | ☐ |
| 7 | Delta feed uses platform-standard opaque cursor / `next_cursor` (the `/memories` keyset shape); resync = cursor-less replay | [COR-2123](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123) | ☐ |
| 8 | `trail_id` stamped at trail merge AND on late upserts whose anchors belong to an already-merged trail (materialized cache of the join) | [COR-2123](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123) | ☐ |
| 9 | Plugin: idempotent per-fact push + pull filtered by HEAD reachability / own session / merged `trail_id` / pool; fixes teammate distribution, no promote step; `lineage.json` cancelled | [COR-2126](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126) | ☐ |
| 10 | Attachment join runs in the BFF at read time; repo page = core on-default commits + merged `trail_id` + pool | [COR-2124](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2124) | ☐ |
| 11 | Pool facts get no special UX — ordinary rows with null provenance columns | [COR-2124](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2124) | ☐ |
| 12 | Measure anchor precision on existing facts before building per-commit rendering; fallback = trail-level rendering for history | [COR-2124](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2124) | ☐ |
| 13 | Trail UI shows memories beside their anchoring commits; repo page shows only main-visible facts; behind `trail-memories`; merged trails keep memories forever, closed-unmerged never reach the repo page | [COR-2125](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2125) | ☐ |
| 14 | Remove the local transcript cache — read transcripts from git checkpoint refs on demand; transient materialization only for backfill | [COR-2128](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2128) | ☐ |

content.thinking:
I'm also considering what happens if the "brain" plugin isn't installed: SpawnDetached re-execs the whole binary with args for "brain memory notify", and the host's plugin dispatcher needs to resolve "brain" to an external plugin binary — so I need to check what happens when that plugin is missing, likely via plugin_on_demand logic.

Since the detached child has no TTY, it can't prompt interactively to install, so it would just error out silently with stdout/stderr discarded — a harmless but wasted short-lived process per commit. I'm also tracing failure modes: the hint never firing if nothing was condensed, spawn failures like os.Executable or cmd.Start errors being swallowed, and child failures like the plugin dispatcher erroring out when the plugin binary is missing.

There's also a guard (ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER=1) preventing the worker's own git/entire invocations from re-triggering notifications, so no infinite recursion even though the notify child shells out to entire for token minting and checkpoint explanation. For stampedes, many sessions condensed in one commit spawn multiple detached processes, but a plugin-side 60-second claim-first throttle collapses them so losers exit quickly; in test binaries, SpawnDetached is a no-op. Now I'm tracing the actual call path: a post-commit git hook invokes `entire hooks git post-commit`, which runs the PostCommit strategy per session.

The hint gets sent not via IPC but by re-executing the entire binary itself as a detached process with specific notify arguments, with no TTY and output discarded, and the plugin dispatcher inside that child resolves and execs the managed brain binary. Now I'm weighing whether a simpler approach exists, starting with the idea of the plugin installing its own git hook but running into the one-hook-per-name limitation since entire already owns post-commit.

I rule out a synchronous call since that would block the commit, and file-watching since inotify on git refs is messy cross-platform. Writing a hint file would also require a resident daemon to be running, which isn't guaranteed, so spawning on demand is really the simplest mechanism that never blocks the commit and works without a background process already running.

I could add a check for plugin presence before spawning to skip wasted processes, but that's a minor optimization worth skipping. For the answer format I'll do a step-by-step narrative, list the failure modes, assess simpler alternatives, and cover the no-daemon case, all in plain language.

content.text:
Here's the full walk, from `git commit` to the plugin, with code references.

**When it gets called.** You commit → git runs the `post-commit` hook `entire enable` installed → `entire hooks git post-commit` → checkpoint capture → `ManualCommitStrategy.PostCommit` loops over the sessions with pending work. For each session whose condensation **actually produced this commit's checkpoint** (`condensed == true`, main's existing signal), it calls `brainnotify.Notify(worktreePath, EventCheckpoint, sessionID, branch)`. It does not fire when nothing condensed (a commit with no AI-session work), during rebase/cherry-pick sequence operations (PostCommit skips lifecycle transitions there — that's the second test), or from inside the Brain worker itself (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER=1` guard, loop prevention).

**How it gets called / sent.** There is no IPC, socket, queue, or file protocol. `Notify` builds the argv `brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id> --branch <b>` — content-free routing metadata, never transcript content — and hands it to `execx.SpawnDetached`, which **re-execs the `entire` binary itself** (`os.Executable()`) as a detached child: new session on Unix, detached process group on Windows, stdout/stderr discarded, cwd set to the repo root, process released so it outlives the hook. Inside that child, the host's normal plugin dispatcher resolves the `brain` verb to the managed entire-brain binary and execs it. So the "event bus" is: spawn one short-lived process that is just another `entire brain …` invocation.

**Failure modes, and what each costs:**

| Failure | Behavior | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `os.Executable()` or `Start()` fails | swallowed, hook unaffected | one missed hint |
| Plugin not installed | child's dispatcher errors; detached child has no TTY, so no install prompt; output discarded | one short-lived no-op process per commit |
| Repo not brain-enabled / brain paused | plugin exits silently (`backgroundPaused`, repo resolution guards) | nothing |
| Plugin crashes mid-work | detached, output discarded | missed hint |
| Condense succeeded but state save failed | hint still fires (it's advisory); worker finds nothing new | one wasted nudge |
| Commit burst (rebase with many commits, many sessions in one commit) | one spawn per condensed session, but the plugin's claim-first 60s throttle collapses them; losers exit in milliseconds | a few empty processes |
| Hint lost for any reason above | the daemon tick and reconciliation pass pick the work up later | staleness only — **a lost hint can never lose data or misplace a fact**, which is the design's one load-bearing property |

**Is there a simpler way?** I looked at the alternatives honestly:

- *Plugin installs its own post-commit git hook*: git allows one hook per name, entire already owns it, chaining is brittle — and the plugin wouldn't know **which session** condensed into the checkpoint. That session↔checkpoint mapping is information only the host has at that moment, and it's the payload that makes the hint useful.
- *Synchronous call inside the hook*: violates the never-block-the-commit rule.
- *Host writes a hint file, plugin daemon picks it up*: avoids the spawn, but only works when a resident daemon is running — and it often isn't. The spawn is what makes this work daemon-free: the notify child itself launches the worker on demand.
- *Do nothing, rely on the daemon tick*: that's the status quo this fixes.

So the spawn is already the minimal mechanism satisfying the four constraints (never block the commit, no resident daemon required, carries the session id, no new protocol). The one marginal simplification available: stat the plugins dir before spawning so a machine without the plugin doesn't pay one empty process per commit — I left it out as a micro-optimization, but it's a two-line add if the empty spawn bothers you.

**If brain is not installed:** `Notify` still spawns (the host deliberately doesn't know about plugin inventory), the child's plugin dispatcher fails to resolve `brain`, the error would normally prompt "install the plugin?" but a detached child can't prompt, so it prints the non-interactive error into the discarded stderr and exits. The commit, the hook, and the user see nothing. Cost: ~one process spawn per condensed session per commit, a few milliseconds. If that's unacceptable, the stat-before-spawn check above removes it.

# Review PR

Review a pull request with structured, actionable feedback.

## Arguments

- `this PR. especially for simplicitiy` — PR number, URL, or branch name. If empty, review the current branch's open PR.

## Process

### 1. Fetch PR context

```
gh pr view <pr> --json title,body,baseRefName,headRefName,additions,deletions,changedFiles,commits,author
gh pr diff <pr>
```

Read the PR description carefully — it defines scope and intent. Everything you review should be evaluated against what the PR is trying to accomplish.

### 2. Understand the change

Before reviewing line-by-line:
- What is this PR doing and why?
- What files are touched and what's the blast radius?
- Are there any architectural implications?

### 3. Review with this checklist

**Correctness**
- Does the code do what the PR description says?
- Are there logic errors, off-by-one bugs, or unhandled edge cases?
- Are error paths handled correctly?

**Security**
- Any injection risks (SQL, XSS, command injection)?
- Are secrets, tokens, or credentials handled safely?
- Are inputs validated at system boundaries?

**Testing**
- Are there tests for the new/changed behavior?
- Do tests cover edge cases, not just the happy path?
- Are test assertions meaningful (not just "doesn't throw")?

**Design**
- Does the change follow existing codebase patterns and conventions?
- Is the abstraction level appropriate (not over/under-engineered)?
- Are there unnecessary changes outside the stated scope?

**Performance**
- Any N+1 queries, unbounded loops, or missing pagination?
- Are there opportunities for batching or caching that were missed?
- Will this scale with the data sizes it will encounter?

**Readability**
- Are names clear and consistent with the codebase?
- Is complex logic adequately explained?
- Would a future reader understand the "why" behind non-obvious decisions?

### 4. Adversarial review

Take a second, adversarial pass over the diff. Actively try to break the change — assume it has flaws and hunt for them across:

- **Performance** — worst-case inputs, hot paths, allocations, contention.
- **Stability** — race conditions, partial failures, retries, resource leaks, crash recovery.
- **Correctness** — inputs and states that violate the author's assumptions.
- **Simplicity** — code that could be deleted or replaced with something simpler/stdlib.
- **Platform design standards** — deviations from the platform's established design patterns and conventions.

Add any findings to the output using the same severity format.

### 5. Run /simplify

Run the `/simplify` skill (via the Skill tool) against the changed code and fold its findings into the review output.

### 6. Structure your output

For each finding, use this format:

**[severity] file:line — short title**
Description of the issue and why it matters. Include a suggested fix when possible.

Severity levels:
- **[blocking]** — Must fix before merge. Correctness bugs, security issues, data loss risks.
- **[important]** — Should fix. Design problems, missing tests for critical paths, performance issues.
- **[nit]** — Nice to fix. Style, naming, minor improvements. Don't block merge on these.
- **[question]** — Not necessarily wrong, but needs clarification or discussion.

### 7. Summary

End with a brief summary:
- Overall assessment (approve / request changes / needs discussion)
- What the PR does well
- Top 1-3 items that need attention
- Any scope concerns (changes that seem unrelated to the stated goal)

## Guidelines

- Review what's in the diff, not what you wish was there. Don't request unrelated refactoring.
- If the PR is large, focus on the most impactful files first.
- Be specific — "this could be better" is not useful. Show what "better" looks like.
- Distinguish between "this is wrong" and "I would do this differently." Only the former is blocking.
- If you're unsure about something, use [question] severity instead of asserting it's wrong.
- Read relevant source files (not just the diff) when you need context about how changed code integrates with the rest of the system.

+// Package brainnotify sends content-free lifecycle hints to the optional
+// Entire Brain plugin without putting plugin work on a host hook's critical
+// path.
+package brainnotify
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
+)
+
+// Event is a lifecycle event understood by `entire brain memory notify`.
+type Event string
+
+const (
+	EventSessionStart Event = "session_start"
+	EventCheckpoint   Event = "checkpoint"
+	EventSessionEnd   Event = "session_end"
+
+	memoryWorkerOriginEnv = "ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER"
+)
+
+var spawnDetached = execx.SpawnDetached
+
+// Notify launches `entire brain memory notify` as detached, best-effort work.
+// The argv is deliberately limited to content-free routing metadata. Repository
+// identity stays owned by Brain, which resolves it from repoRoot.
+//
+// Notify has no result by design: a missing or failing Brain plugin must never
+// change the host hook's result or output. Canonical reconciliation repairs a
+// missed hint later.
+func Notify(repoRoot string, event Event, sessionID, branch string) {
+	if os.Getenv(memoryWorkerOriginEnv) == "1" {
+		return
+	}
+	if strings.TrimSpace(repoRoot) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(sessionID) == "" || !event.valid() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	args := []string{
+		"brain", "memory", "notify",
+		"--event", string(event),
+		"--session", sessionID,
+	}
+	if branch != "" {
+		args = append(args, "--branch", branch)
+	}
+
+	spawnDetached(repoRoot, args...)
+}
+
+func (e Event) valid() bool {
+	switch e {
+	case EventSessionStart, EventCheckpoint, EventSessionEnd:
+		return true
+	default:
+		return false
+	}
+}

+	sessionID string

+
+func captureBrainCheckpointHints(t *testing.T) *[]capturedBrainCheckpointHint {

+			repoRoot:  repoRoot,
+			event:     event,
+			sessionID: sessionID,
+			branch:    branch,
+		})
+	}
+	return &hints

+	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	hints := captureBrainCheckpointHints(t)

+	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)

+	files := []string{"brain-a.txt", "brain-b.txt"}

+		setupSessionWithCheckpointAndFile(t, s, dir, sessionID, files[i])
+		state, loadErr := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
+		require.NoError(t, loadErr)
+		state.Phase = session.PhaseIdle
+		state.FilesTouched = []string{files[i]}
+		require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))
+	}
+
+	commitFilesWithTrailer(t, repo, dir, "abc123def456", files...)
+	require.NoError(t, s.PostCommit(context.Background()))
+
+	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(context.Background())
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	branch := GetCurrentBranchName(repo)
+	require.Len(t, *hints, 2)
+	gotSessions := []string{(*hints)[0].sessionID, (*hints)[1].sessionID}
+	slices.Sort(gotSessions)
+	slices.Sort(sessionIDs)
+	require.Equal(t, sessionIDs, gotSessions)
+	for _, hint := range *hints {
+		require.Equal(t, repoRoot, hint.repoRoot)
+		require.Equal(t, brainnotify.EventCheckpoint, hint.event)
+		require.Equal(t, branch, hint.branch)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestPostCommitDoesNotSendCheckpointHintWhenCondensationIsSkipped(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	hints := captureBrainCheckpointHints(t)
+
+	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
+	sessionID := "brain-checkpoint-skipped"
+	setupSessionWithCheckpoint(t, s, repo, dir, sessionID)
+
+	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	state.Phase = session.PhaseActive
+	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

+func createRebaseMarker(dir string) error {
+	return os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, ".git", "rebase-merge"), 0o755)

+// Package brainnotify sends content-free lifecycle hints to the optional
+// Entire Brain plugin without putting plugin work on a host hook's critical
+// path.
+package brainnotify
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
+)
+
+// Event is a lifecycle event understood by `entire brain memory notify`.
+type Event string
+
+const (
+	EventSessionStart Event = "session_start"
+	EventCheckpoint   Event = "checkpoint"
+	EventSessionEnd   Event = "session_end"
+
+	memoryWorkerOriginEnv = "ENTIRE_BRAIN_MEMORY_WORKER"
+)
+
+var spawnDetached = execx.SpawnDetached
+
+// Notify launches `entire brain memory notify` as detached, best-effort work.
+// The argv is deliberately limited to content-free routing metadata. Repository
+// identity stays owned by Brain, which resolves it from repoRoot.
+//
+// Notify has no result by design: a missing or failing Brain plugin must never
+// change the host hook's result or output. Canonical reconciliation repairs a
+// missed hint later.
+func Notify(repoRoot string, event Event, sessionID, branch string) {
+	if os.Getenv(memoryWorkerOriginEnv) == "1" {
+		return
+	}
+	if strings.TrimSpace(repoRoot) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(sessionID) == "" || !event.valid() {
+		return
+	}
+
+	args := []string{
+		"brain", "memory", "notify",
+		"--event", string(event),
+		"--session", sessionID,
+	}
+	if branch != "" {
+		args = append(args, "--branch", branch)
+	}
+
+	spawnDetached(repoRoot, args...)
+}
+
+func (e Event) valid() bool {
+	switch e {
+	case EventSessionStart, EventCheckpoint, EventSessionEnd:
+		return true
+	default:
+		return false
+	}
+}

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.text:
Review complete, fixes pushed to the PR (`f7d95bbf6`), both package suites green, checkout restored to main. The structured review:

## Review: entireio/cli#2784 — simplicity focus

**[important] strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go — hint bypassed the save gate — FIXED**
The hint fired in the loop body after `MutateSessionStateOnSaved` returned, so it fired even when the save failed or skipped. That mechanism's doc (session_state.go:560) explicitly names "detached process spawn" as an intended `onSaved` effect, and `condensedTelemetry.emit` right next to it honors the discipline. Moved the hint into the `onSaved` callback — simpler *and* more correct. (Altitude agent; I had wrongly rationalized this as "advisory, harmless" in the original PR.)

**[important] strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:70 — seam var orphaned a doc comment — FIXED**
My insertion landed between `errPromptTimedOut`'s doc comment and its declaration. Three of four agents flagged it independently. Moved.

**[nit] brainnotify — dead event surface — FIXED**
`EventSessionStart`, `EventSessionEnd`, the `Event` type, and the `valid()` switch had zero production callers (session-end is deprecated as a trigger; the compiler already prevents the mistake `valid()` guarded). Collapsed to one function, `NotifyCheckpoint(repoRoot, sessionID, branch)` — the package is now ~55 lines, and the events return with their call sites if ever.

**[nit] brainnotify — fork per commit on plugin-less machines — FIXED**
Brain is optional, so "not installed" is the common case, and each condensed session cost a full `entire` re-exec that only discovered the plugin is missing. Added a `LookPath("entire-brain")` guard (verified: main.go prepends the managed plugin dir to PATH, so this resolves managed installs) — a stat instead of a fork.

**[nit] strategy — `GetCurrentBranchName(repo)` per loop iteration — FIXED**
One `.git/HEAD` read + ref resolution per session for a value that can't change mid-PostCommit. Hoisted above the loop.

**[question] one spawn per condensed session — SKIPPED, deliberate**
Batching into one spawn per commit needs a repeatable `--session` flag on the plugin side (cross-repo contract change), the plugin's 60s claim-first throttle already collapses the burst, and multi-session commits are rare. Not worth the contract churn now.

**[nit] worker-origin env var owned by the other repo — ADDRESSED via comment**
The plugin's own notify handler is the real recursion guard (verified in `memory_cmd.go`); the host-side check is now documented as a spawn-cost optimization, so a plugin-side rename can't silently remove protection.

**Clean:** reuse (correctly uses `execx.SpawnDetached` and matches the repo's seam-var conventions — `sweepSpawn`, `trailRefreshSpawn`), mechanism altitude (no generic host→plugin event bus exists to reuse; `PostCommit` is the right layer since both condense paths converge there and only the host knows session+branch at that moment).

**Summary: approve, with the five fixes now in the PR.** The PR does the core thing right — detached, never-fails, content-free, reuses existing machinery — and the review made it ~90 lines lighter and save-gated. {"id":"COR-2127","uuid":"41ca52f6-58da-4f99-b940-cc2b470c9db8","title":"Checkpoint event: host brainnotify → plugin, primary trigger for distill + fact sync","description":"Part of the <issue id="d61511dc-1e5b-4864-b8b6-11b36b7af5d3" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110/design-how-memories-attach-to-trails-upload-scope-triggers-edge-cases">COR-2110</issue> design (v3). The checkpoint event becomes the **primary** trigger for both distill and fact sync. Session-end is being deprecated (developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never); nothing new may depend on it.

**Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

1. `entire enable` installs a post-commit git hook that runs `entire hooks git post-commit` — this is the existing checkpoint-capture path in the host CLI.
2. Inside that flow the host calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. Detached and never-fails by design: a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. This host half exists on the **unmerged** entireio/cli branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` (commit 73a92e8da) — land or re-cut it.
3. The plugin endpoint (`entire brain memory notify`, on main in `internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`) records a content-free hint and nudges the plugin's worker.
4. The worker runs, throttled: distill the transcript delta since the previous checkpoint (anchoring facts to the checkpoint window they came from — better precision than session-end distill, which lumps the whole session onto its last checkpoint), then push the fact store.

**Interaction with** <issue id="755307d8-ec2e-45eb-ac93-fcf1a3abc157" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123/brainstore-per-fact-storage-with-anchors-upsert-delta-feed-endpoints">COR-2123</issue>**/2126:** none structurally — the trigger is transport-agnostic. Before the per-fact storage/client land, the hint fires the existing branch-head sync; after <issue id="1adb7ab6-393d-4506-be10-44c6e0763800" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces">COR-2126</issue>, it fires the upsert/pull client. **Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/evisdrenova/.claude/plugins/cache/entire-skills/entire/0.7.2/skills/address-findings

# Address Findings

Fix and resolve the open review findings on an Entire trail. A finding is a
review comment posted to a trail on entire.io: it has a file/line location, a
body, a severity, and sometimes a suggested unified-diff patch. This skill
fetches the open findings, applies or hand-fixes each one in the current
worktree, and marks it resolved on the trail.

## When to use / not use

Use when the user points at a trail — a URL like
`https://<host>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<number>/<slug>`, or a bare trail
number or branch — and asks to **address / fix / resolve** its findings or
review comments.

Do **not** use this skill for:

- A code review of the current diff — that is the `review` skill (read-only).
- Creating new findings — use `entire trail finding add`.

## Response Format

Begin the first response to this skill invocation with the line:

`Entire Address Findings:`

followed by a blank line, then the content. Apply the header to the **first
response only**. Omit it on error / early-exit responses (CLI missing, not
authenticated, trail not found, branch mismatch, no open findings).

## Rules

1. Make the smallest correct change that addresses each finding. Do not expand scope.
2. Only mark a finding resolved when you actually addressed it. If a finding is
   ambiguous or needs a human decision, leave it open and report it.
3. Do not commit or push. Leave changes in the working tree for the user to review.
4. Never weaken a test or assertion just to clear a finding.

## Process

### 1. Verify the CLI

Run `entire version`. If the command is not found, stop and tell the user:
"The Entire CLI is required but not installed. Install it from
https://entire.io/docs/cli and try again."

### 2. Resolve the trail selector

- If the argument is a trail URL, take the number from the `/trails/<number>/`
  path segment and use that number.
- If it is a bare trail number, id, or branch name, use it as-is.
- If you cannot determine a trail, stop and ask the user for the trail URL or number.

Use this value as the `<trail>` selector for every command below. `entire trail`
accepts a trail number, id, or branch name interchangeably, so no number lookup
is needed — a branch name works directly.

### 3. Fetch open findings

```bash
entire trail finding list <trail> --json --status open
```

- If the output reports that authentication is required, stop and tell the user:
  "`entire trail finding list` requires authentication. Run `entire login` and try again."
- If the `trail finding` subcommand is unavailable, or the API reports the
  feature is not enabled, stop and tell the user that trail findings may not be
  enabled for this account or repository. Do not invent findings.
- Parse the JSON. Each finding has an id, a severity, a status, a body, a
  location (file path + line range), and may include a suggested change (a
  unified diff).
- If there are no open findings, report "No open findings on this trail." and stop.

### 4. Branch guard (you must be on the trail's branch)

`entire trail finding apply` edits the local worktree, so you must be on the
trail's branch before changing files.

```bash
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD                # current branch
entire trail list --json --status any -n 200   # locate the trail's branch
```

Find the trail whose `number` or `branch` matches your selector and read its `branch`.

- If the trail's branch differs from the current branch, stop and tell the user:
  "Trail `<trail>` targets branch `<trail-branch>`, but you are on
  `<current-branch>`. Check it out first (`entire trail checkout <trail>`) and
  re-run." Do not edit files.
- If you cannot find the trail in the list (e.g. pagination), do not hard-fail:
  warn that you could not verify the branch, and ask the user to confirm they are
  on the trail's branch before you continue.

### 5. Address each finding

Process findings highest severity first (high → medium → low). For each:

1. **If it has a suggested unified-diff change**, dry-run it first:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding apply <trail> <finding-id> --check
   ```

   If it applies cleanly, apply and resolve in one step:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding apply <trail> <finding-id> --resolve
   ```

2. **Otherwise** (no patch, the patch conflicts, or the fix needs reasoning):
   read the finding body, open the file at its location, and make the smallest
   correct edit that addresses it. If a fast, relevant local check exists for the
   touched code (a build or a focused test), run it. Then resolve:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding resolve <trail> <finding-id> -m "<one line: what you changed>"
   ```

3. **If you cannot confidently address it** (ambiguous, needs a product/design
   decision, or out of scope): leave it open, do not resolve it, and record it
   for the report.

### 6. Report

Summarize:

- Resolved via suggested patch — list finding ids and files.
- Resolved via manual edit — list finding ids, files, and a one-line of what changed.
- Left open for your decision — list finding ids and why.
- Any errors encountered.

Remind the user the changes are uncommitted and ready for review.

## Failure modes

- **CLI not installed** → install message (step 1).
- **Not authenticated** → "`entire trail finding list` requires authentication. Run `entire login` and try again."
- **Trail findings not enabled / API error** → tell the user the feature may be
  unavailable; do not fabricate findings.
- **Trail not found** → tell the user to check the URL or number; suggest
  `entire trail list --status any`.
- **Wrong branch** → stop with the checkout instruction (step 4).
- **Patch does not apply** → fall back to a manual edit; if you cannot fix it
  confidently, leave the finding open and report it.
- **Not a git repository** → stop and tell the user to run from inside the trail's repo.

content.thinking:
Checking the findings, cli #1581 has zero open findings since the unresolved count is just a discussion thread. But entire-brain #290 has one high-severity finding worth digging into: it flags that `hostedSyncOnCheckpointHint` runs synchronously inside `memory notify`'s RunE, though since the host spawns notify detached, the commit itself isn't blocked.

The deeper issue is that `memory notify` is meant to be a fast, content-free hint, but this inline call makes the notify process run distill operations with long timeouts and unbounded network round-trips — a host adapter that invokes notify synchronously could block for minutes, even though today's host spawns it detached. The proper fix is to dispatch this work through the existing async machinery instead of running it inline, likely by spawning a detached process similar to how memoryWorkerLaunch works, rather than bolting it onto the existing worker queue.

I'm now sketching the concrete plan: have the notify handler spawn a detached self-invocation of a new hidden command (something like `hook checkpoint-sync`) that runs the sync logic inline in the child, reusing the throttle marker to dedupe. content.text:
Because decision 3 as we recorded it said "checkpoint is the primary trigger for **both distill and sync**" — that's what I implemented. But your challenge is right, and it's the same thing the trail finding was circling: the event path should be dumb. Distill timing doesn't affect correctness anywhere in the v3 design — facts anchor to their checkpoint whenever they're distilled, and attachment is a read-time join — so coupling token-spending agent work to the commit beat buys freshness at the cost of putting the most expensive, least reliable step (needs an agent on PATH, minutes of runtime) inside an event handler chain.

One consequence to keep eyes on: distill has to live *somewhere*. Today it's session-end (default-on) + daemon tick (opt-in). Once session-end is removed, if checkpoint doesn't distill either, nothing creates distilled facts by default. The structurally right home is the **memory worker** the notify already nudges — distill as a durable worker job with its own cadence and budget, which is exactly the async dispatch the trail finding asked for. That belongs to the session-end-deprecation work, not this PR.

I'm also keeping the per-chunk distill cache even though the event no longer distills: it has standalone value today (a resumed session ends more than once, and each session-end re-distilled the whole transcript — the cache makes that one tail chunk), and it's the prerequisite for worker-driven per-checkpoint distill later.

1	# Design: how memories attach to trails (COR-2110)
2	
3	Version 3, approved 2026-10-14. Owner: evis. Implementation tickets: COR-2123 to COR-2127. Versions 1 and 2 are summarized at the end.
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	A fact records which session, checkpoint, and commit produced it. These provenance anchors are written at creation and never change. Every consumer — the trail page, the repo Memories page, and a teammate's local brain — selects facts by querying these anchors. The branch name is not a key anywhere. Sync is per-fact: the client upserts facts up, and pulls a repo-wide delta down, filtered locally by git reachability from its own HEAD. Upload runs on the checkpoint event (per commit), on session end, and on the daemon tick.
8	
9	## Problem
10	
11	Memories are keyed by branch name at every layer:
12	
13	- Local store: `facts/<slug>-<sha256(branch)[:4]>/facts.ndjson` (`internal/cli/facts.go`).
14	- Sync protocol: `GET/POST /api/v1/repos/{repoID}/brain/facts?branch=<name>` (`internal/factsync/httpserver.go`), one CAS set-head per `(repo, branch)`.
15	- Brainstore: `branch` is in the primary key of `brain_fact_heads`, `brain_facts`, and `brain_fact_events`. `/memories` filters `WHERE repo_id = $1 AND branch = $2`.
16	
17	Branch names change. Three failure modes, all reported:
18	
19	1. Rename (Conductor renames placeholder branches automatically): local facts stay in the old directory; the hosted head stays under the old name; the new name starts empty.
20	2. Delete after merge: the rows still exist under the old name, but no caller holds that name, so the trail UI gets an empty list.
21	3. Recycle: a new branch that reuses a deleted name syncs against the old head. The first pull imports the old facts into the new local store, and new facts publish into the old head.
22	
23	A fourth problem surfaced during this design: with per-branch heads and no promote step, facts synced under a feature branch never enter the `main` head, so a teammate on main never receives them locally after the trail merges. Version 1 papered over this with a promote-on-merge event. Version 3 fixes it structurally.
24	
25	## Facts about the current system that the design uses
26	
27	- Fact identity is `sha256(normalized text + sorted paths)`. Branch is not part of the identity (`factmerge/record.go`).
28	- Fact status moves one way: active → superseded/retracted. Never back.
29	- Distill stamps each fact with provenance anchors: SessionID, CheckpointID, transcript position (`internal/cli/distill_cmd.go:1133`). It does NOT stamp `Anchor.Commit` today; only authored facts get a commit (`rememberAnchorCommit`, `internal/cli/facts_write_cmd.go`). The design requires distill to also stamp the commit, resolved from the fact's OWN checkpoint via the `Entire-Checkpoint` commit trailer (the entity index already builds this mapping from git log) — never from HEAD: a background distill of an old session must anchor to that session's historical commit, not whatever is currently checked out. An unresolvable checkpoint leaves the commit blank; an absent anchor is honest, a wrong one is not (same rule as `rememberAnchorCommit`). Part of COR-2126.

32	- The platform already maps checkpoints and sessions to trails. Trails have stable ULIDs.

34

36	
37	One rule everywhere: a fact is selected by its anchors, never by a branch name.
38	
39	Ingestion is one funnel: `remember` and distill (kept as-is — decided 2026-10-14) both write the local fact store. The fact store pushes to brainstore on post-commit. 40	
41	### Storage (brainstore)
42	
43	Per-fact rows keyed `(repo_id, fact_id)`, plus anchor rows (fact_id → SessionID, CheckpointID, Commit, TurnID). No set heads, no CAS, no `branch` column in any key. Branch may be stored as display metadata on an anchor.
44	
45	Writes are idempotent upserts: anchors union, status advances one way, text/paths are fixed by the content-derived ID. Two clients upserting the same fact converge without coordination. Conflicting facts (two active facts that disagree) are stored side by side; resolution belongs to the planned async pipeline, same as before.
46

63	- A lost event delays an upload. It cannot misplace a fact, because selection is computed from stored anchors at read time.
64	
65	### Attachment (which trail or page shows a fact)
66	
67	- A fact belongs to trail T if any anchor references a session, checkpoint, or commit in T. The UI renders the fact next to the commit its anchor points to.

{"id":"COR-2127","uuid":"41ca52f6-58da-4f99-b940-cc2b470c9db8","title":"Checkpoint event: host brainnotify → plugin, primary trigger for distill + fact sync","description":"Part of the <issue id="d61511dc-1e5b-4864-b8b6-11b36b7af5d3" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110/design-how-memories-attach-to-trails-upload-scope-triggers-edge-cases">COR-2110</issue> design (v3). The checkpoint event is an **upload beat only**: it syncs the existing fact store to brainstore, detached and throttled. It does NOT distill (corrected 2026-10-15 — the event path stays cheap and agent-free; distill timing never affects correctness because facts anchor to their checkpoint whenever distilled). Fact creation stays on session-end + daemon tick and moves into the memory worker with the session-end deprecation. Session-end is being deprecated (developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never); nothing new may depend on it.

**Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

1. `entire enable` installs a post-commit git hook that runs `entire hooks git post-commit` — this is the existing checkpoint-capture path in the host CLI.
2. Inside that flow the host calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. Detached and never-fails by design: a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. This host half exists on the **unmerged** entireio/cli branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` (commit 73a92e8da) — land or re-cut it.
3. The plugin endpoint (`entire brain memory notify`, on main in `internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`) records a content-free hint and nudges the plugin's worker.
4. notify spawns a detached, hidden `memory checkpoint-work` verb (same launch shape as the memory worker; worker-origin child env for loop protection), which claims a shared 60s throttle marker and pushes the fact store for the hinted branch + default branch. Nothing heavy runs inline in notify — a host adapter may invoke it synchronously (this was also a trail-review finding on trail 290, now resolved).
5. Shipped alongside (prerequisite for later worker-driven per-checkpoint distill, and immediate savings for resumed sessions that end repeatedly): the per-chunk distill cache — a grown transcript re-dispatches only its new tail chunks.

**Interaction with** <issue id="755307d8-ec2e-45eb-ac93-fcf1a3abc157" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123/brainstore-per-fact-storage-with-anchors-upsert-delta-feed-endpoints">COR-2123</issue>/2126: none structurally — the trigger is transport-agnostic. Before the per-fact storage/client land, the hint fires the existing branch-head sync; after <issue id="1adb7ab6-393d-4506-be10-44c6e0763800" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces">COR-2126</issue>, it fires the upsert/pull client. This ticket can land first.

{"id":"COR-2127","uuid":"41ca52f6-58da-4f99-b940-cc2b470c9db8","title":"Checkpoint event: host brainnotify → plugin, detached fact-store upload (+ per-chunk distill cache)","description":"Part of the <issue id="d61511dc-1e5b-4864-b8b6-11b36b7af5d3" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2110/design-how-memories-attach-to-trails-upload-scope-triggers-edge-cases">COR-2110</issue> design (v3). The checkpoint event is an **upload beat only**: it syncs the existing fact store to brainstore, detached and throttled. It does NOT distill (corrected 2026-10-15 — the event path stays cheap and agent-free; distill timing never affects correctness because facts anchor to their checkpoint whenever distilled). Fact creation stays on session-end + daemon tick and moves into the memory worker with the session-end deprecation. Session-end is being deprecated (developers leave sessions running for days, so it fires late or never); nothing new may depend on it.

**Where the event comes from and how it is triggered:**

1. `entire enable` installs a post-commit git hook that runs `entire hooks git post-commit` — this is the existing checkpoint-capture path in the host CLI.
2. Inside that flow the host calls `brainnotify.Notify`, which spawns a detached `entire brain memory notify --event checkpoint --session <id>` through the plugin dispatcher. Detached and never-fails by design: a missing or broken plugin cannot affect the commit or the hook's output. This host half exists on the **unmerged** entireio/cli branch `feat/brain-lifecycle-hints` (commit 73a92e8da) — land or re-cut it.
3. The plugin endpoint (`entire brain memory notify`, on main in `internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`) records a content-free hint and nudges the plugin's worker.
4. notify spawns a detached, hidden `memory checkpoint-work` verb (same launch shape as the memory worker; worker-origin child env for loop protection), which claims a shared 60s throttle marker and pushes the fact store for the hinted branch + default branch. Nothing heavy runs inline in notify — a host adapter may invoke it synchronously (this was also a trail-review finding on trail 290, now resolved).
5. Shipped alongside (prerequisite for later worker-driven per-checkpoint distill, and immediate savings for resumed sessions that end repeatedly): the per-chunk distill cache — a grown transcript re-dispatches only its new tail chunks.

**Interaction with** <issue id="755307d8-ec2e-45eb-ac93-fcf1a3abc157" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2123/brainstore-per-fact-storage-with-anchors-upsert-delta-feed-endpoints">COR-2123</issue>/2126: none structurally — the trigger is transport-agnostic. Before the per-fact storage/client land, the hint fires the existing branch-head sync; after <issue id="1adb7ab6-393d-4506-be10-44c6e0763800" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces">COR-2126</issue>, it fires the upsert/pull client. This ticket can land first.
